title: The Little Match Girl
author: Hans Christian Andersen (安徒生)
summary: 大年夜寒风刺骨，赤足的小女孩在雪地里叫卖火柴。在饥寒交迫中，她一次次擦亮微弱的火柴，在神奇的火光中看到了温暖的火炉、肥美的烤鹅、美丽的圣诞树与唯一疼爱她的慈祥祖母。

paragraphs.author: Hans Christian Andersen (安徒生)
paragraphs.en:
The Little Match Girl
Hans Christian Andersen (安徒生)
paragraphs.zh: 《卖火柴的小女孩》 · Hans Christian Andersen (安徒生)

paragraphs.en: Most terribly cold it was; it snowed, and was nearly quite dark, and evening—the last evening of the year. In this cold and darkness there went along the street a poor little girl, bareheaded, and with naked feet.
paragraphs.zh: 天气冷得可怕，大雪纷飞，夜幕低垂，这是一年中的最后一个夜晚——除夕之夜。在这刺骨的寒冷与漆黑之中，一个贫苦的小女孩光着脑袋，赤着双脚，孤独地在街头踽踽独行。

paragraphs.en: When she left home she had slippers on, it is true; but they had been her mother's, so large were they; and the poor little thing lost them as she scuffled away across the street, because of two carriages that rolled by dreadfully fast.
paragraphs.zh: 离家出门时她确实是穿着拖鞋的，可那是她母亲穿过的旧鞋，实在太宽大了。当两辆马车在马路上风驰电掣般飞奔而过时，可怜的小姑娘吓得慌忙逃窜，结果两只大拖鞋全跑丢了。

paragraphs.en: So the little maiden walked on now with her tiny naked feet, that were quite red and blue from cold. She carried a quantity of matches in an old apron, and she held a bundle of them in her hand. Nobody had bought anything of her the whole livelong day; no one had given her a single farthing.
paragraphs.zh: 于是，小姑娘只好赤着一双小脚往前走，娇嫩的双脚早已冻得又红又青。她用破旧的围裙兜着一大堆火柴，手里还紧紧攥着一小把。整整一整天，没有一个人向她买过一根火柴，也没有人施舍给她哪怕一个铜子儿。

paragraphs.en: Shivering through cold and hunger she crept along; a picture of misery, poor little girl! The flakes of snow covered her long fair hair, which fell in beautiful curls around her neck; but of that, of course, she never once thought now. Lights were shining from every window, and there was a savory smell of roast goose, for it was New Year's Eve—yes, of that she thought.
paragraphs.zh: 她又冷又饿地瑟瑟发抖，一步一步向前挪动，真是一幅凄凉无比的凄苦景象！纷纷扬扬的雪花落满她金黄柔顺的长发，在颈边卷曲出美丽的波浪，然而她此刻根本无暇顾及这些。家家户户的窗扉里都透出温暖明亮的灯光，空气中弥漫着烤鹅扑鼻的香气——因为今晚是大年夜啊，是的，她脑海里全萦绕着这烤鹅的香味。

paragraphs.en: In a corner between two houses she sat down and huddled herself together. She had drawn up her little feet under her, but she grew colder and colder; and to go home she did not venture, for she had not sold any matches and could not bring a farthing of money: from her father she would certainly get blows.
paragraphs.zh: 在两座房屋相交凹陷的墙角里，她蜷缩着坐了下来。她把一双小脚蜷在裙下，可身体还是越来越冷、越来越僵。她实在不敢迈步回家，因为她没卖出一根火柴，连一个子儿都没挣到，回去必定会招来父亲的一顿毒打。

paragraphs.en: Her little hands were almost dead with cold. Ah! a match might do her good, if she might but dare to draw one out of the bundle, and rub it against the wall, and warm her fingers. She drew one out. R-r-r-itch! how it spirted, how it burnt! It was a warm, bright flame, like a candle, as she held her hands over it: a wonderful little light that was!
paragraphs.zh: 她的一双小手几乎冻僵得没了知觉。啊！哪怕只有一根火柴该多好啊，只要她敢从整把火柴里抽出一根在墙上一擦，就能暖和暖和手指了。她终于小心翼翼抽出一根。“哧！”火柴燃起来了，冒出欢快的火星！当她把两只小手罩在火苗上时，那是一团多么温暖明亮的烛光啊，真是一束神奇绝妙的微光！

paragraphs.en: The girl thought she sat before a large iron stove, with burnished brass feet and a brass ornament at top. The fire burnt with such blessed influence; it warmed so delightfully! But the little flame went out, the stove vanished, and she had only the remains of the half-burnt match in her hand.
paragraphs.zh: 小女孩仿佛置身于一座带有锃亮黄铜炉脚和精美铜顶的大铁火炉前。炉火烧得旺极了，散发出无比神圣温馨的暖意，让人感到那么舒服！然而火苗骤然熄灭，大铁炉也随之烟消云散，她手里只剩下一小截烧焦的火柴梗。

paragraphs.en: She rubbed another against the wall: it burnt brightly, and where the light fell on the wall, there the wall became transparent like a veil, so that she could see into the room. On the table was spread a snow-white tablecloth; upon it was a splendid roast goose, stuffed with apples and dried plums, which smoked terribly and deliciously.
paragraphs.zh: 她又在墙上擦亮了第二根火柴：火光映照之处，冰冷的砖墙变得如轻纱般透明，她竟能一眼看清房间里的摆设。餐桌上铺着雪白的台布，上面摆着一只油汪汪、塞满了苹果与李子干的美味烤鹅，正散发着浓郁诱人的热气。

paragraphs.en: And what was still more capital to behold was, the goose hopped down from the dish, reeled about on the floor with knife and fork in its breast, till it came to the poor girl; when—the match went out and the thick, cold, damp wall was alone before her.
paragraphs.zh: 更令人惊奇的是，那只烤鹅竟从盘子里扑棱棱跳了下来，胸膛上插着刀叉，摇摇晃晃地沿着地板朝可怜的小女孩径直走来；然而——火柴又熄灭了，眼前唯有一面厚重、冰冷而潮湿的高墙。

paragraphs.en: She lit another match. Now there she was sitting under the most magnificent Christmas tree: it was still larger, and more decorated than the one which she had seen through the glass door at the rich merchant's. Thousands of lights were burning on the green branches, and coloured pictures looked down upon her.
paragraphs.zh: 她又点燃了第三根火柴。这一次，她发现自己正端坐在最豪华璀璨的圣诞树下：这棵树比她透过大富商玻璃门看到的还要高大、还要光彩夺目。碧绿的松枝上点缀着数以千计的明亮烛火，五彩缤纷的精美画片正俯身凝视着她。

paragraphs.en: The little maiden stretched out her hands towards them—when the match went out. The lights of the Christmas tree rose higher and higher, she saw them now as stars in heaven; one fell down and formed a long trail of fire. 'Someone is just dead!' said the little girl; for her old grandmother, the only one who had loved her, and who was now no more, had told her, that when a star falls, a soul ascends to God.
paragraphs.zh: 小姑娘兴奋地朝它们伸出双手——火柴又熄灭了。圣诞树上的烛光越升越高，化作了夜空中闪烁的繁星；突然一颗流星划破夜空，拖出一道长长的火线。“有人刚刚死去了！”小女孩喃喃低语道；因为唯一疼爱过她、如今早已辞世的老祖母曾告诉过她：每当有一颗流星陨落，便有一具灵魂升入了上帝的怀抱。

paragraphs.en: She drew another match on the wall: it was often light around her, and in the brightness stood her old grandmother, clear and radiant, yet mild and happy. 'Grandmother!' cried the little one. 'Oh, take me with you! I know you will go away when the match burns out; you will vanish like the warm stove, the delicious roast goose, and the great glorious Christmas tree!'
paragraphs.zh: 她又在墙上擦亮了一根火柴：柔和的光晕笼罩四周，在那片光明之中，慈祥的老祖母伫立在那里，面容神圣而光彩夺目，温和慈爱地微笑着。“祖母！”小女孩动情地呼喊道，“噢，带我一起走吧！我知道火柴一熄灭你就会不见的；就像那温暖的火炉、肥美的烤鹅和美丽的圣诞树一样消失得无影无踪！”

paragraphs.en: And she rubbed the whole bundle of matches quickly against the wall, for she wanted to be quite sure of keeping her grandmother near her. And the matches gave such a brilliant light that it was brighter than at noon-day: never formerly had the grandmother been so beautiful and so tall. She took the little maiden, on her arm, and both flew in joy and in splendour, far, far above the earth, to where there was neither cold, nor hunger, nor pain: they were with God.
paragraphs.zh: 为了能把祖母长久留在身边，她急切地把整把整把的火柴全擦亮了。火柴迸发出万道炽烈璀璨的光芒，把四周照耀得比正午还要明亮晃眼！祖母从未像此刻这般美丽慈祥、高大端庄。老祖母将小姑娘紧紧拥入怀中，两人在无尽的喜悦与祥光中高高飞升，飞向那没有严寒、没有饥饿、也没有苦难痛苦的极乐之地——她们与上帝同在。

paragraphs.en: In the cold morning light there sat the little girl, in the corner between the houses, with red cheeks and a smile on her mouth: she had frozen to death on the last evening of the old year. 'She wanted to warm herself!' people said. No one imagined what beautiful things she had seen, nor into what glory she had entered with her grandmother, on New-year's Day.
paragraphs.zh: 在元旦清晨刺骨冰冷的阳光下，小女孩依旧静静坐在两座房屋相交的墙角里，两腮泛着红晕，嘴角挂着宁谧甜美的微笑——她已在旧年的最后一个寒夜里冻死了。“她肯定是想暖和暖和自己吧！”围观的人们叹息道。可谁也不曾想到，她曾经亲眼目睹过多么绚丽神圣的美景；谁也不曾知晓，她已同亲爱的祖母一道，在璀璨无瑕的光辉中迎来了新年的黎明。
